title: Post-rollout follow-ups: remove v1-only selector paths + document kernel registry update process
creator: Connor O'Brien
description:
Context
- Selector v2 is now rolled out (default-on for Hosted; Dedicated opt-in per rollout ticket) with the kill switch + per-family overrides in place.
- We intentionally left some selector v1-specific scaffolding and duplicated config paths during rollout to make rollback safe and reduce blast radius.

This follow-up ticket cleans up the deprecated v1-only codepaths and documents the operational update process for kernel registry entries so that future additions (new model families, new GPUs, better kernels) are predictable and don’t require tribal knowledge.

Scope
A) Code cleanup (post-rollout)
1) Remove / isolate v1-only selection code
- Identify remaining call sites that directly instantiate selector v1 or branch on v1-only heuristics.
- Keep v1 implementation available as an explicit fallback (for kill switch), but eliminate:
  - duplicated config parsing paths
  - v1-only logging/metrics dimensions that are no longer emitted
  - dead code for “legacy kernel id mapping” (if registry is authoritative)
- Ensure we preserve deterministic fallback behavior: v2 -> safe kernel set -> v1 (as last resort), but make it explicit and testable.

2) Consolidate config + override precedence
- Validate we have one canonical precedence order documented + reflected in code:
  (a) emergency kill switch (global)
  (b) per-cluster override (Dedicated / Private)
  (c) per-model-family override
  (d) registry table default
  (e) v1 fallback only if v2 cannot produce a safe selection
- Remove any legacy env vars / config keys that were only used for v1 canarying.

3) Delete/rename deprecated flags + add guardrails
- Deprecate old flags with a clear error if set (fail-fast at startup with message + migration hint).
- Add “smoke test” unit coverage to ensure no one can accidentally reintroduce the deprecated v1 branch via config.

B) Documentation / process: kernel registry entry lifecycle
Create a single “how to update the registry” doc that covers:
- Ownership + review: Runtime Kernels (Hiro/Grace) owns registry contents; changes require perf evidence and conformance sign-off.
- How entries are generated/edited:
  - where the registry file lives
  - required fields (model family id, seq bucket, GPU SKU normalization key, kernel id, safe/experimental marker, minimum SM capability)
  - versioning and compatibility rules (what constitutes breaking vs non-breaking change)
- Required validation before merge:
  - benchmark-lab run across the relevant GPU matrix + prompt distributions
  - conformance tests for representative shapes (incl. NaN/overflow guard)
  - telemetry/cardinality check for any new labels/fields
- Promotion process:
  - experimental -> canary -> default
  - rollback plan (which override to use; who to page)
- Where to look in observability to confirm impact:
  - selector version breakdown
  - kernel-choice heatmap
  - p95 latency and tok/s by model family + seq bucket + GPU

Out of scope
- Adding new kernels.
- Changing customer-facing semantics.
- Reworking scheduler integration; only cleanup + docs.

Acceptance criteria
- Runtime builds without deprecated v1-only config keys; startup fails with a clear message if old keys are present.
- Selector v2 remains default, and the kill switch still reliably forces v1 (verified by a unit/integration test).
- Metrics remain within cardinality standards; no duplicate kernel selection metrics emitted.
- New doc exists and is linked from:
  - runtime kernel registry architecture page
  - selector override/rollback runbook
  - release notes addendum (internal)

Implementation notes / pointers
- Start by grepping for:
  - selector_v1, legacy_selector, v1_only, KERNEL_SELECTOR_LEGACY, old config keys referenced in rollout PRs
- Coordinate with:
  - Grace Kim (selector logic expectations)
  - Benji Okafor (flag/config cleanup)
  - Allison Grant / Thomas Baird (telemetry + cardinality standards)

Links
- Rollout execution: ENG-3934
- Config/feature flags: ENG-3931
- Registry schema/versioning: ENG-3926
- Telemetry standards: kernel-selection-telemetry-standards (Confluence)
- Override/rollback runbook (Confluence)
comments: 2026-02-20 (Connor O'Brien): Capturing cleanup+process work as a standalone ticket so it doesn’t get lost after rollout. Please prioritize removing deprecated config keys before the next runtime cut; we already had one customer ask which flag to use (they were looking at an old snippet).

2026-02-22 (Grace Kim): +1. Please keep v1 available behind the kill switch, but let’s remove the “heuristic layering” path that was only there to compare v1/v2 in-prod; it’s confusing and makes traces harder to interpret.

2026-02-24 (Thomas Baird): When you consolidate metrics, ensure we do not emit both kernel_choice and legacy_kernel_choice. The legacy series is a cardinality trap when combined with model id. Bucket to model_family + gpu_sku + seq_bucket only.

2026-02-25 (Kira Thompson): I can take the doc/process portion and partner with Grace for the technical details. For code cleanup, suggest we split into a sub-task if it looks bigger than expected once we enumerate remaining call sites.
